notes: Hand-curated from a tools/tubuild.py create starting point. The generator's five review items were all resolved here: func_ov015_02111ce0's own extern "C" block is kept as written; the func_ov015_02111fb8, dBgActor_c::UpdateModelPosAndRotY and dBgActor_c::UpdateClsnPosAndRot declarations were reconciled to one spelling each (the void return, which is what include/dBgActor_c.h declares); and the pointer-to-member typedef was restored to the Behavior file's spelling, which is the one the state dispatch needs.

NAME. The cartridge's own _ZTS at ov015:0x0211451c spells 19daObjBk_Dossunbar_c, and the _ZTI/_ZTV chain at 0x02114510/0x0211458c binds it to this vtable. The tree's previous name MovingBar was COINED -- it occurs nowhere in the 9.0 MiB extracted cartridge, case-sensitive or case-folded, while Dossunbar occurs in both the RTTI string and the arm9 profile ids BK_DOSSUNBAR_L / BK_DOSSUNBAR_S. The rename was applied with tools/class_rename.py and the _ZTV row in config/arm9/overlays/ov015/symbols.txt was renamed in place at its unchanged address 0x0211458c; no alias row was added anywhere.

SINIT FOLD (2026-10): the handwritten src/unnamed/ov015/__sinit_ov015_02113048.c is retired; this TU now defines the four file handles and the two seven-entry PMF dispatch tables the initializer fills, so mwcc emits __sinit_d_a_obj_bk_dossunbar.cpp itself. SharedFilePtr has no fields or ctor, so model handles use DossunbarModelFilePtr (func_02017acc/func_02017ab4) and collision handles use DossunbarCollisionFilePtr (func_02017b4c/SharedFilePtr_Destruct_Clsn); the manifest aliases each wrapper spelling to the arm9 destination. The 14 PMF literals emit as compiler-local .data records (@736..@768, four renumbered via defined_symbol_renames for cross-module collisions) and the enter-table PMF data_ov015_02114a24 is walked raw by func_ov015_02111fb8. All fifteen state/installer functions are daObjBk_Dossunbar_c methods now (PMF records prove membership). production_mode intact-object: this entry licenses .init/.ctor/.data/.bss alongside .text.

THE FOURTEEN STATE FUNCTIONS KEEP THEIR ADDRESS-DERIVED NAMES ON PURPOSE. Nothing in the cartridge names them, so renaming them would be a name-recovery act rather than a codegen one, and each of the thirteen state bodies is the target of a pointer-to-member record in UNOWNED .data that dsd resolves by symbol NAME: a rename that does not reach config/arm9/overlays/ov015/symbols.txt in the same commit links that record as zero and no byte gate at any stage reports it. Converting them to real members is the next concrete improvement for this class, not part of this promotion.

DESTRUCTOR. include/daObjBk_Dossunbar_c.h gives the destructor an INLINE empty body and declares it ahead of the out-of-line virtuals, which is what makes mwcc emit D1 at 0x02111ba0 then D0 at 0x02111be4 and no D2 -- exactly what the cartridge carries. That inline body is also why this TU emits the eleven vague-linkage RTTI records licensed in compiler_only_output. Writing the destructor out of line instead flips the pair to D0-before-D1 and adds a homeless D2. The two legacy destructor shards had to leave the build in this same change, because an inline body in the header redefines what an enrolled out-of-line shard defines and that is a COMPILE error, not a link one.

tools/tubuild.py verify reports 23/25 and criterion relocation_destinations_verified FAIL. Both DIFF lines are the single message `_ZTV19daObjBk_Dossunbar_c: unexpected reloc type=2 addend=0` on the two factories, and criterion every_declared_function_bytes_match is PASS -- no byte differs. That message comes from tools/objisolate.py's one-function isolation route, whose externalise branch accepts only addend >= 8 while its consolidated route accepts addend 0 as the ROM-symbol convention. Measured at this revision, the already-promoted ov015 siblings daObjBkBillboard_c (6/7) and daObjBk_Rotebar_c (6/7) report the identical message on their own factories, so it is a property of that route and not of this class. What settles it is the production route: tools/tubuild.py linkcheck links all 25 functions into the real ov015 range with 0 differing bytes, 106/106 modules exact, 0 new dsd check symbols errors against the baseline control, and a linked ROM byte-identical to the stock control.
